az802-q-281.objective: Define the recovery point objective as the maximum acceptable data-loss window measured in time.
keyPoints: RPO bounds how much data change the business can afford to lose after an incident.
RPO is set per workload and directly shapes replication and backup frequency.
An RPO of 15 minutes means at most roughly 15 minutes of lost changes.
whyOthers: Restoring service within a deadline is RTO, a different objective.
Domain-controller counts have no relationship to data-loss tolerance.
Backup disk size is capacity planning, not a time-based loss bound.

az802-q-282.objective: Define the recovery time objective as the target time to restore service after disruption.
keyPoints: RTO bounds how quickly service must be back after an incident.
RTO drives stand-up runbooks, automation, and failover design.
RPO and RTO together define the overall continuity requirement.
whyOthers: Password age describes account-lifecycle policy, unrelated to service restoration.
DNS caching duration controls record refresh, not recovery timing.
Maximum file size is a storage limit, not a recovery objective.

az802-q-283.objective: Explain that differential backups capture all changes since the last full backup.
keyPoints: Differential backups grow until the next full backup resets the delta base.
Restore needs the last full plus the latest differential.
Compared with incrementals, differentials trade more storage and copy time for simpler restores.
whyOthers: Mirror-only checkpoints are Hyper-V state capture, not a backup type.
Incremental backups capture changes since the previous backup of any type, not since the full.
Synthetic delete is not a recognized backup taxonomy term.

az802-q-284.objective: Explain that incremental backups capture changes since the previous backup of any type.
keyPoints: Incrementals are the smallest and fastest daily runs but chain restore steps.
Restore requires the last full plus each needed incremental in order.
Any single damaged increment can break the whole restore chain.
whyOthers: Differential backups always delta from the last full backup, not from yesterday's media.
A full-only scheme re-copies everything daily, the opposite of incremental efficiency.
Replica metadata describes replication state, not backup deltas.

az802-q-285.objective: Prove recoverability with actual restore exercises, not just successful backup jobs.
keyPoints: A completed backup job proves capture, not that a restore meets RTO or data requirements.
Restore tests validate media integrity, procedures, permissions, and application dependencies.
Schedule drills and track their duration against RTO.
whyOthers: Test frequency does not change the size classification of backups.
Restore testing and monitoring answer different questions; neither replaces the other.
Encryption state is independent of whether restores are exercised.

az802-q-286.objective: Design backups with protected, access-controlled, tested copies including isolated or immutable storage.
keyPoints: Keep at least one copy an attacker cannot reach or overwrite: isolated or immutable.
Restrict access to backup administration with privileged accounts and separate credentials.
Regularly test restores so the defense is proven, not assumed.
whyOthers: One shared administrator account is an easy single point of compromise.
Disabling alerts hides the biggest signal that an attack is underway.
Storing the only backup on the production server defeats the purpose entirely.

az802-q-287.objective: Use system state backups to capture critical AD DS, registry, and boot components of a domain controller.
keyPoints: System state includes AD DS, SYSVOL, registry, boot files, COM+ class registry, and certificates.
It supports nonauthoritative restores of directory components without full-volume recovery.
wbadmin start sytemstatebackup -backupTarget:... runs an ad-hoc system-state capture.
whyOthers: Screenshots are not a recoverable OS state.
User folders live in volume backups, not in the state database.
DHCP lease data is its own targeted backup, not part of system state.

az802-q-288.objective: Recognize DSRM as the offline recovery environment for the AD DS database.
keyPoints: DSRM boots a DC with directory services stopped so ntdsutil and restore tools can act offline.
The DSRM Administrator password is distinct from domain credentials and must be recorded securely.
Recovery mode selection happens through boot options or WBC/VM configuration.
whyOthers: DHCP configuration happens online with the DHCP console or PowerShell.
Cluster joining is a generic HA action with no directory-recovery semantics.
DNSSEC signing operates on zones online, unrelated to DSRM.

az802-q-289.objective: Distinguish nonauthoritative restore (receive updates from partners) from authoritative restore (replicate restored data outward).
keyPoints: Nonauthoritative restore pulls newer state from replication partners; it is the default correction path.
Authoritative restore pushes selected data (for example deleted OUs) out to partners.
Choose by deciding whether the restored copy is the source of truth, not just recovery mechanics.
whyOthers: Schema and DNS roles are independent; the restore modes are not about them.
The two modes are operationally very different, not identical.
Printer restoration is an ordinary workload restore, not an AD concept.

az802-q-290.objective: Use authoritative SYSVOL restore when the restored copy must repopulate policy and scripts to other DCs.
keyPoints: Authoritative SYSVOL restore marks the restored content as the domain's copy to replicate outward.
Use the msDFSR-Options attribute (or BurFlags D2) to force authoritative SYSVOL sync.
For forest recovery, perform authoritative SYSVOL on the first reinstated DC only.
whyOthers: SYSVOL holds policy and scripts; DNS zone data lives elsewhere.
SYSVOL restore never creates a forest automatically.
Removing Group Policy objects is a separate administrative task, not SYSVOL restore semantics.

az802-q-291.objective: Explain that failover clustering continues supported workloads on another node after failure.
keyPoints: Clustered roles fail over to surviving nodes with limited or no downtime for supported roles.
Instructions live in the cluster database and are kept consistent by quorum.
Failover clustering is distinct from replication or backup as an availability mechanism.
whyOthers: Clustering does not remove the need for patching; rolling upgrades coordinate but do not eliminate it.
DNS recursion is a resolver concern with no clustering tie.
Backups remain mandatory; HA is not a substitute for restore capability.

az802-q-292.objective: Prevent split-brain by requiring sufficient quorum votes or a proper quorum model.
keyPoints: Quorum defines how many votes are required to keep operating, preventing partitions from acting independently.
Convert a lost vote into a witness (disk, file share, or cloud) to keep quorum reachable.
A cluster without sufficient votes goes offline to protect consistency.
whyOthers: Every node running DHCP is a service distribution choice, not a quorum mechanism.
Returning multiple addresses from DNS can add ambiguity, not cluster-safe decisions.
VM checkpoints are point-in-time virtualization state, not cluster voting.

az802-q-293.objective: Use a witness as an additional tie-break vote in quorum decisions.
keyPoints: Witnesses add a tie-breaking vote: file-share witness or cloud witness are common for two-node clusters.
Choose witness type based on topology; they help maintain quorum, not participate in workload.
A witness stores only minimal cluster information, never user data.
whyOthers: Witnesses never store passwords; storing secrets there would be unsafe.
VM memory allocation is a resource-setting concern, not a quorum artifact.
Encrypting shares is an SMB protocol-level function, not witness behavior.

az802-q-294.objective: Use planned maintenance failover to move workloads deliberately to another node.
keyPoints: Planned failovers drain roles to another node before maintenance, minimizing disruption.
Use it to validate every node's ability to host roles before unscheduled failovers.
Coordinate cluster patching through planned failover and rolling upgrades.
whyOthers: Deleted user objects are not recovered by cluster moves; restore them from backups or the Recycle Bin.
Disabling monitoring is unrelated and increases operational risk.
Deleting the cluster database destroys configuration, an anti-pattern during maintenance.

az802-q-295.objective: Describe in-place upgrade as upgrading the existing OS installation while retaining supported roles and settings.
keyPoints: In-place upgrade keeps hardware, roles, and settings while moving to a newer release.
Validate compatibility, confirm working backups, and plan rollback before starting.
Some roles or applications require dedicated migration steps instead of in-place upgrade.
whyOthers: Converting an RODC to DNS is not a real upgrade path.
Creating a new forest automatically is not part of any upgrade operation.
Replacing a file server with Azure Files is a service migration, not an OS upgrade.

az802-q-296.objective: Prefer side-by-side migration when you need a rollback path, hardware refresh, or a clean configuration on a new server.
keyPoints: A parallel target server allows staged migration, testing, and controlled cutover.
Hardware refresh and redesign usually choose this path instead of in-place upgrade.
Decommission the old server only after validation completes.
whyOthers: When no new server can be provisioned, side-by-side is exactly the path that cannot run.
Unsupported applications need remediation regardless of migration approach.
Unavailable backups block every safe path rather than selecting one.

az802-q-298.objective: Apply security translation during a file-server migration so migrated accounts retain access to resources.
keyPoints: ACLs grant access through SIDs; SID history keeps original SIDs valid in the token during migration.
Security translation rewrites resource ACLs to reference the new domain's SIDs.
Run translation after confirming group memberships so no access is lost at cutover.
whyOthers: Converting VHDX to VHD is a disk-image conversion, unrelated to access control.
DHCP option translation adjusts network settings, not permissions.
Resolving DNS names into IPs is name resolution, not identity migration.

az802-q-299.objective: Assess dependencies, runtime compatibility, data stores, authentication, networking, and performance requirements before migrating an IIS workload to Azure.
keyPoints: Map application dependencies first; a web server is never only web files.
Confirm runtime and database compatibility along with authentication design.
Network and performance requirements drive sizing and connectivity decisions.
whyOthers: DNS TTL is a single record lifetime setting, not a migration assessment.
The server hostname carries over trivially and proves nothing about readiness.
Local user counts reveal nothing about application dependencies.

az802-q-300.objective: Finish recovery or migration work with documented tests, business validation, monitoring, and runbook updates.
keyPoints: Validated behavior, not a completed copy, is what makes a service ready.
Runbooks must reflect the current tested environment so future recovery repeats success.
Monitor recovered or migrated services and close gaps found during validation.
whyOthers: Deleting the source before validation creates an unrecoverable failure mode.
Disabling alerts removes the signal needed to catch post-cutover problems.
Assuming a successful copy means readiness ignores real functional proof.

az802-q-297.objective: Use Active Directory Migration Tool (ADMT) to migrate AD DS objects between domains or forests.
keyPoints: ADMT migrates users, groups, and computers, supporting security translation scenarios.
Trusts between source and target domains are a prerequisite for object migration.
Plan password migration and SID history usage for phased restructuring.
whyOthers: Disk Cleanup removes unneeded files; it never migrates directory objects.
DNS Manager manages name records, not users, groups, or computers.
Hyper-V Replica replicates whole VMs and cannot migrate AD objects.
